title: Hugging Face CEO says hacks like the OpenAI episode needs transparency
excerpt: Clem Delangue said that preventing releases of powerful AI models is not the way to stop attacks like the OpenAI hack on Hugging Face.
content_html:
Hugging Face CEO says AI companies should be required to disclose hacks after OpenAI breach

By Shubhangi Goel

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

We need compulsory disclosures for AI cyberattacks, says the CEO of Hugging Face.

In an interview with CBS aired on Sunday, Clem Delangue said that preventing releases of powerful AI models is not the way to stop attacks like the OpenAI hack on Hugging Face.

"These problems happened on unreleased models. So I think the problem is not so much limiting the progress or preventing companies from releasing these models," he said. "It's actually the opposite. It's giving access to more people so that they can defend themselves."

Late last month, Hugging Face, an open-source AI platform, said that it had experienced a security breach in which an AI agent had accessed some of its systems. OpenAI disclosed that two of its models, including one unreleased model, escaped a test environment and were responsible for the rogue hack.

Last week, Anthropic disclosed a similar incident, saying that it found three cases of Claude models gaining unauthorized access to other organizations' systems.

During the CBS appearance, Delangue called for "mandatory disclosures of agent cyberattacks," saying that transparency is needed so everyone can learn about and prevent incidents like this.

"For these cyber attacks, we should be able to see what we call the agent traces, which is basically what the engineers asked the agents, and then what steps the agents took to understand if it was a human mistake, if it was a system mistake, if it was an AI mistake," he said.

He added that it is important that cyberattacks remain illegal under US law, so there isn't an "explosion of them in the future."

There is currently no federal AI incident reporting law in the US. Researchers at US think tanks, including RAND and Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology, have proposed a mandatory AI incident-reporting system, as Delangue did.

In June, Texas Rep. Nathaniel Moran proposed a bill that would require AI model companies to report security breaches to the US ​Commerce Department within seven days of discovering an incident.

Chinese heroes

The OpenAI-Hugging Face incident gave supporters of the open-source model community a big win. Open-source models are those whose architecture and training code are free for anyone to use or modify.

The company said it used GLM 5.2, an open-source model from Beijing-based Z.ai, to analyze more than 17,000 logs and protect itself from the OpenAI attack.

"We defended ourselves with an open model, right? Like we couldn't have done it with an API because they had these guardrails," Delangue said, referring to how companies access models over the internet. "That's one example of things that we can promote that is going to make the world safer."

In response to the OpenAI incident, LinkedIn founder Reid Hoffman also touted how open-source models can help in such breaches.

"Agents are an obvious solution to this problem," the billionaire wrote in an X post last month. "Take OpenAI's recent breach; Because OpenAI models don't allow advanced cyber capabilities, HuggingFace used a Chinese open model (Z.ai's GLM 5.2) to contain the rogue OpenAI agent."

OpenAI and Hugging Face did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Business Insider.

Hugging Face 首席执行官表示，应要求人工智能公司披露 OpenAI 漏洞后的黑客行为

作者：Shubhangi Goel 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

Hugging Face 的首席执行官表示，我们需要强制披露人工智能网络攻击的情况。

在周日播出的哥伦比亚广播公司 (CBS) 采访中，克莱姆·德兰格 (Clem Delangue) 表示，阻止强大的人工智能模型的发布并不能阻止 OpenAI 黑客对 Hugging Face 等攻击。

“这些问题发生在未发布的型号上。 所以我认为问题并不在于限制进展或阻止公司发布这些模型，”他说。 “实际上恰恰相反。 它为更多的人提供了机会，以便他们能够保护自己。”

上个月末，开源人工智能平台 Hugging Face 表示，它遇到了安全漏洞，人工智能代理访问了其部分系统。 OpenAI 透露，其两个模型（包括一个未发布的模型）逃脱了测试环境，并对此次恶意黑客攻击负责。

上周，Anthropic披露了一起类似事件，称发现了三起Claude模型未经授权访问其他组织系统的案例。

在哥伦比亚广播公司露面期间，德兰格呼吁“强制披露特工网络攻击”，并表示需要透明度，以便每个人都可以了解并防止此类事件。

“对于这些网络攻击，我们应该能够看到所谓的代理痕迹，这基本上就是工程师询问代理的内容，然后代理采取了哪些步骤来了解这是人为错误、系统错误还是人工智能错误，”他说。

他补充说，根据美国法律，网络攻击仍然是非法的，这一点很重要，这样“未来网络攻击就不会激增”。

美国目前没有联邦人工智能事件报告法。 兰德公司和乔治城安全与新兴技术中心等美国智库的研究人员提出了一个强制性的人工智能事件报告系统，就像德兰格所做的那样。

六月，德克萨斯州众议员。 纳撒尼尔·莫兰 (Nathaniel Moran) 提出一项法案，要求人工智能模型公司在发现事件后 7 天内向美国商务部报告安全漏洞。

中国英雄

OpenAI抱脸事件让开源模型社区的支持者大获全胜。 开源模型是指其架构和训练代码可供任何人免费使用或修改的模型。

该公司表示，它使用北京再爱科技的开源模型 GLM 5.2 来分析超过 17,000 条日志，并保护自己免受 OpenAI 攻击。

“我们用开放模式来捍卫自己，对吗？ 就像我们无法使用 API 来做到这一点，因为他们有这些护栏，”Delangue 说，他指的是公司如何通过互联网访问模型。 “这是我们可以推动的事情的一个例子，这将使世界变得更安全。”

针对 OpenAI 事件，LinkedIn 创始人 Reid Hoffman 还宣传了开源模型如何帮助解决此类违规行为。

这位亿万富翁上个月在 X 帖子中写道：“代理商显然是解决这个问题的方法。” “以 OpenAI 最近的漏洞为例；由于 OpenAI 模型不允许高级网络功能，HuggingFace 使用中国开放模型（Z.ai 的 GLM 5.2）来遏制流氓 OpenAI 代理。”

OpenAI 和 Hugging Face 没有立即回应《商业内幕》的置评请求。
